public_rationale: Several components face material problems. The located 11% report concerns FY2027 Q1, Microsoft reported rising total revenue, and CNBC reported a later $15 billion raise before publication. The $10.9 billion figure is an operating loss. Earlier reporting does document $11 billion received. These findings should not be collapsed into one matched financial result: the sentence omits accounting bases and combines distinct periods and metrics.
limitations: Unresolved does not mean the individual assertions are equally plausible.
Private-company financing and loss figures rely on reporting rather than accessible primary financial statements.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI made up 11% of Microsoft's total revenues in Q1 FY2026, which the author says suggests Microsoft's overall revenues are in decline and its AI revenues aren't filling the gap outside OpenAI, which lost $10.9 billion in Q3 2026 and raised only $11 billion of the $30 billion it wanted at a $1.25 trillion valuation, lower than expected.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI made up 11% of Microsoft’s total revenues in Q1 Fiscal Year 2026, which suggests that Microsoft’s overall revenues are in decline and that its AI revenues aren’t filling the gap

from_speaker: Microsoft’s overall revenues are in decline
AI revenues aren’t filling the gap outside of an AI lab
raised only $11 billion of the $30 billion it wanted
our_interpretation: Preserve the stated fiscal year; do not silently substitute FY2027.
Read overall revenue decline as a decline in revenue level, ordinarily year over year.
For the ongoing revenue assertion, use the latest reportable quarter before publication, July–September 2026.
Read the unqualified loss as net loss unless its source establishes another basis.
Read raised as funding completed by publication, distinguishing money received from promised later tranches.
The single metric_scope records the financing component. Revenue share, revenue trend, loss and valuation require separate measurements and cannot be treated as one financial metric.
Suggests expresses an inference, not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Separate, period-matched records substantiate the revenue share, decline, non-OpenAI AI revenue gap, loss, completed financing, target and valuation comparison.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched records materially refute a stated component; a mixed assessment requires independently established supporting and contradicting components.

evidence.explanation: The latest quarter's total revenue increased year over year. This conflicts with the ordinary reading of overall revenue decline, but does not isolate non-OpenAI AI revenue.

evidence.excerpt: (Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.)
evidence.explanation: The article associates the nearly 11% figure with FY2027 Q1. That does not establish the same share for the explicitly claimed FY2026 Q1.

evidence.excerpt: The ChatGPT maker’s operating loss for the period was $10.9 billion.
evidence.explanation: Supports the existence of the reported number, but identifies an operating loss rather than a net loss. It cannot settle an unqualified net-loss reading.

evidence.excerpt: About $11 billion in new money reached OpenAI's accounts by Friday, November 6, 2026, people familiar with the deal said.
evidence.explanation: Documents the earlier $11 billion close. The article describes further tranches and reports that the CFO disputed the higher initial valuation attributed to the company.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI raises $15B at a $1.25T valuation, sources say.
evidence.explanation: Later reporting conflicts with treating $11 billion as the latest raised amount on November 17. The accessible text does not reconcile committed funds with cash received.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Separate component contracts, the relevant Microsoft customer-revenue disclosures, OpenAI's loss definition, and a dated reconciliation of funding received and committed through November 17.
